[Regulation] Article 1 (Definition) “Child” refers to a minor. Article 2 (Physical Child Abuse) Anyone who commits an act of physical abuse by assaulting a child or causing harm to his or her physical health and development shall be punished by imprisonment for not more than 5 years. Article 3 (Sexual Child Abuse) Anyone who commits an act of sexual abuse causing sexual humiliation to a child shall be punished by imprisonment for not more than 6 years. <Review Opinions> Alice: Crimes of child abuse are distinct from general violent crimes in that the guardian, who has a duty of care, inflicts harm upon the person to be protected. Bob: The [Regulation] aims to thoroughly punish the perpetrators of abuse and thereby provide strong protection for children, who are the victims of various abusive acts. Therefore, the subject of the acts in Articles 2 and 3 should be retained as “anyone” as in the current regulation. Charlie: In relation to sexual acts, child victims cannot be treated in the same way as adult victims who possess sexual self-determination. (c). The research finding that “recently, cases where minors make sexual requests to other minors, involving the filming of videos, are increasing. Experiences of responding to such requests without any sense of shame or discomfort critically influence the later development of negative self-identity or distorted sexual awareness. Therefore, the need to punish sexual requests between minors as acts of abuse is great”—this research finding supports both Bob and Charlie’s opinions.

The research team performed this surgery (bariatric surgery) on 608 severely obese patients and observed that, among those with both severe obesity and diabetes, 83% showed improved blood sugar levels. Incretin is a substance secreted by the small intestine when food is consumed, which signals the pancreas to secrete insulin.
